built: orbit now writes decision records only while a setting that reads them is on: a granted chain key, a sign-off setting of change or program, or a tripwire set to halt. A new command, orbit decisions status, says whether records are written and which settings read them. Each workflow skill's body now carries only the basic content of the decision-writing rule: run that command at each command's first step and again after the session edits the project config, and follow the rule when it says records are written. The rule itself moved, every clause kept but its opening one, into the reference file each skill ships. The skill bodies are about 34,000 characters smaller, and the budget test's ceilings were lowered to match.
seams: No new question is asked. One setting-dependent behaviour is new: with none of the three reading settings on, the AI writes no new ledger entry or stop record, and with any of them on it writes them as before. Whatever the settings, an answer to a stop already in a change's history, or a fix of a record already there, is still written.
deviations: Two, both decided in the proposal review and walk (D-rbs-10): the charter says that at the defaults the AI writes no resolution, but a resolution answering a stop already in a trail, and a replacement fixing a record already there, are still written, so turning the last reading setting off strands no stop; and the charter says the review's reading step selects nothing at the defaults, which holds only on a trail with no records, since records written earlier are still read and fixed. The command reports write and readers rather than whether records are owed, because owed already means a record awaiting its reading.

defines.definition: an orbit command that reads the project settings and says whether decision records are written, and which settings read them
a change's folder of run records, where its decision records are kept
